reasoning: Recent general‑election polling of the Michigan U.S. Senate race in late July and early August 2026 consistently shows a narrowly Republican‑tilting contest between GOP nominee Mike Rogers and Democratic nominee Abdul El‑Sayed, with most surveys in the field over the last 45 days putting Rogers ahead by low‑single‑ to low‑double‑digit margins, and one poll showing only a 4‑point edge within the margin of error.[2][11][14][15] Taken together, these credible statewide polls suggest the current Senate general‑election environment in Michigan is approximately R+5–7, meaning Republicans hold a modest advantage but the race remains competitive.[2][11][14][15] Michigan’s structural partisan baseline from the Cook Partisan Voting Index is EVEN, indicating no long‑term lean toward either major party at the statewide level.[13]

sources.name: Breitbart summary of Glengariff Group Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Glengariff Group statewide poll of likely Michigan voters found Mike Rogers leading Abdul El‑Sayed 49%-39% in the 2026 U.S. Senate general election, a 10‑point Republican advantage.

sources.name: Newsweek on Glengariff Group Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Newsweek’s write‑up of the same Glengariff Group poll reports Rogers leading El‑Sayed 49%-39% among 600 likely voters, describing it as the largest recent GOP edge in the Michigan Senate race.

sources.name: Newsweek on EPIC-MRA Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: An EPIC-MRA poll of 600 likely Michigan voters showed Mike Rogers ahead of Abdul El‑Sayed 46%-43% in the Senate general election, a 3‑point Republican lead within the margin of error.

sources.name: Newsweek on Mitchell Research Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Mitchell Research & Communications poll of 672 likely Michigan voters found Rogers and El‑Sayed tied at 45%-45% in the Senate general election, indicating an even race at that moment.

sources.name: Jewish Insider on Michigan Senate hypothetical matchups
sources.details: Jewish Insider’s coverage of a Michigan Senate poll reported Haley Stevens leading Mike Rogers by 2 points (47%-45%) while Abdul El‑Sayed trailed Rogers by 7 points in separate hypothetical general‑election matchups.

sources.name: WJR on Michigan Education/Glengariff Senate poll
sources.details: WJR’s summary of a survey aligned with Glengariff Group/Business Leaders for Michigan reported Rogers with a 10‑point lead over El‑Sayed in a hypothetical Senate matchup, reinforcing a mid‑single to double‑digit GOP edge.

sources.name: Fox News Poll on Michigan Senate race
sources.details: A Fox News survey of Michigan registered voters found Mike Rogers leading Abdul El‑Sayed 51%-47% in the Senate race, a 4‑point Republican edge that the outlet notes is within the survey’s margin of error.

sources.name: The Hill on EPIC-MRA Michigan Senate trial heats
sources.details: The Hill’s write‑up of an EPIC-MRA survey of 600 likely Michigan voters noted that Haley Stevens was slightly ahead of Mike Rogers in general-election trial heats while Rogers remained highly competitive, underscoring a closely divided electorate.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling on Michigan Democratic Senate primary
sources.details: Emerson College Polling/WLNS/WOOD-TV survey of 700 likely Democratic primary voters showed Abdul El‑Sayed leading Haley Stevens 54%-39% (57%-41% including leaners) for the Michigan Democratic Senate nomination.

sources.name: New York Times overview of Michigan Democratic Senate primary polls
sources.details: A New York Times polling roundup cited multiple Democratic‑primary polls (Zenith, SoCal Strategies, Emerson, Tavern, Tulchin) all showing El‑Sayed with double‑digit leads over Stevens in the Senate primary, typically between 10 and 19 points.

sources.name: MLive on Tavern Research Michigan Democratic Senate primary poll
sources.details: MLive reported a Tavern Research poll of 914 likely Democratic primary voters putting El‑Sayed ahead of Stevens 46%-36% in the Senate primary, a 10‑point margin.

sources.name: Newsweek on final Michigan Democratic Senate primary polls
sources.details: Newsweek’s primary‑focused analysis summarized late July surveys (Mitchell, Zenith, Emerson, Tavern) showing El‑Sayed leading Stevens by roughly 10–18 points in the Democratic Senate primary.

sources.name: Wall Street Journal on Michigan Democratic Senate primary results
sources.details: The Wall Street Journal reported that Abdul El‑Sayed ultimately won the Michigan Democratic Senate primary over Haley Stevens 48.5% to 47.5%, indicating a razor‑thin 1‑point victory despite earlier double‑digit polling leads.
